nodes-documentnode.name: NodeView
nodes-documentnode.description:
A document (`Node::Document`, Ratatui `widgets::paragraph`; Ink nodes/index.tsx DocumentNode, reached through
NodeView as the shell reaches it): lines of styled text, wrapped between words to the pane, or cut at the edge when
`cut` is set (Ratatui ignores `cut` today; Ink honours it). In a settings detail it scrolls in its pane
(`scrolls`), with the scrollbar on the frame's border.

**Use it** for prose and facts with no rows to choose: a settings field's explanation, "can it merge?", a set-up
page.

**States:** wrapped, cut, scrolling (settings detail), empty.

**Rules:** section headings inside it are muted bold capitals (`widgets::heading`); label/value facts align at the
longest label plus two.

The story's `node` is the document the host sent; width and height in `ctx` come from the pane.

nodes-listnode.name: ListNode
nodes-listnode.description:
A row list (`Node::List`, Ratatui `ui::rows::RowList`): selectable rows, each with words at the left, an optional
word at the right (`right`) and a `detail` dropped whole when it does not fit. A heading row (`ListRow.heading`)
is never selected; the cursor steps over it.

**Use it** for a nav pane's views, a settings section's rows and any flat choice of places. Use a table for items
with columns, a tree for nested items.

**States:** selected with the keys (bold emphasis on the selection background across the row), selected without
the keys (the quieter selection), plain rows, a heading, a row being edited in place (`editing`).

**Rules:** the selection is the background across the whole row, never a marker glyph (no `›`, `▶`). Counts at
the right are `data.number`, plain words. Keys `↓ ↑ Home End PgDn PgUp` move over headings.

nodes-lognode.name: LogNode

A log (`Node::Log`, Ratatui inline loop plus `ui::scroll::scrollbar`): long output such as a job's trace, with a
terminal's colours mapped to theme slots (`LogPaintLine` runs), sections that fold under their titles, `/` matches

**Rules:** colours come from the slots the host mapped the ANSI colours to, never the raw ANSI; folded sections
read `─ … ⋯ n lines`, no chevrons. Keys: `/` search, `n`/`N` between matches, `+`/`-` fold.

nodes-meterlines.name: NodeView
nodes-meterlines.description:
The stage bar (`Block::Meter` in a `Node::Rich`, Ratatui `ui::meter::stages`; Ink nodes/index.tsx MeterLines,
reached through NodeView): the steps of a run across the width, a bar of `▀` over each stage's mark and name, each
in the stage's look (its run state's tone). It sits under a PIPELINE section (`Block::Section`).

**Use it** under a PIPELINE heading in a detail pane or an item page, for a pipeline's or a workflow's stages.

**States:** each stage by its `Mark` (done ✓, failed ✗, running ●, waiting ◷, manual ▷, stopped ⊘, skipped »);
names cut to the stage's share of the width; no stages draws nothing.

**Rules:** the marks read without colour; the colour is the stage's look, a theme slot. No pill or round caps on
the bars.

**Data gap:** every recorded view (ink/test/fixtures) carries `"stages": []`, so this story shows the real detail
pane where the meter sits, with an empty bar. A surface with stages (a merge request page's Pipeline tab) recorded by
tests/view_fixtures.rs and tests/ratatui_cells.rs would give both renderers' pictures of a filled bar.

The story's `node` is the whole rich node of the pane, as the host sent it.

nodes-tablenode.name: TableNode
nodes-tablenode.description:
A table (`Node::Table`, Ratatui `ui::table::Table`): a flat list of one kind of row with column headings and a
cursor. Columns come from `ColumnSpec` (the same `Columns` a tree uses, so a column means the same in both), are
dropped by `keep` rank as the width shrinks, and values that do not fit are cut with `…`.

**Use it** for a page's list of items or a history of runs, where every row is the same kind. Use a tree when rows
group under others.

**States:** rows with the cursor row selected, empty (the `empty` words in place of rows), columns dropped when
narrow.

**Rules:** headings are muted bold capitals; the selection is the background across the row; no counts in tab
labels above it (the tab says "Merge requests", not "Merge requests · 1", #33).

nodes-treenode.name: TreeNode
nodes-treenode.description:
The banded tree (`Node::Tree`, Ratatui `ui::tree::BandedTree`): the one tree every part uses for nested data
(groups, then sources, then items). Each row has a name, cells in the tree's columns (aligned at every depth and
dropped by `keep` rank as the width shrinks), optional chips after the name, and a `detail` shown whole or not at
all.

**Use it** when rows group under others and folding helps (a tenancy, its repositories, their merge requests). Use
a table when the rows are one kind.

**States:** open (tree lines `├─ └─ │` show what is open), folded (the row ends in `⋯ n`, the count of rows it
holds), selected (the selection background across the whole row, bold emphasis text), selected without focus (a
quieter background when another pane has the keys), group rows on the heading band.

**Rules:** no chevrons (▸ ▾ › ⌄) and no `[+]`/`[-]` for folding: the tree lines and `⋯ n` say it. No left-edge
stripes for new work (the group stripe `▌` is on its way out, #45). Selection is the background across the row,
never a marker glyph. Keys: `space` toggles a fold, `+`/`=` open, `-` closes or goes to the parent.

Width and height in `ctx` come from the pane the story draws it in.

text-chips.name: TextLine

overlay shade, one space each side: ` ` + the icon and its gap in the icon's own colour + `words ` in the tone's

text-diffview.name: DiffView
text-diffview.description:

**Rules:** the cursor mark `▎` is in the gutter cell, not a stripe down the rows; tints and token colours are theme
slots (`diff.added`, `diff.removed`). Ink draws only rows in view.

chrome-menubox.name: MenuBox
chrome-menubox.description:
A menu or a question (`MenuView`, Ratatui `shell/menu.rs`), over the body: a framed box with a title, then each
choice with its key, label and line; headings (HISTORY) are never chosen; a question (`question: true`) is a
dialog whose choices are buttons. It sits where a context click opened it (`at`) or centred.

**Use it** through the host: `x` opens the place's actions menu, a write asks a question before it is sent. A part
contributes choices; it never draws a menu.

**States:** a choice highlighted (the selection background across the row), a heading, a choice with no key, a
question with buttons, a typed field, scrolled (`PgUp/PgDn`), too small to use.

**Command palette:** Ctrl-P searches commands. `palette` adds the matched/total count, highlights the host's
matched label graphemes in bold accent, and puts shortcuts against the right edge. Typing, scrolling, pointer
targets, scrim, and shadow use the same menu. Long labels wrap without losing a command's target.

**Rules:** the box clears what is under it (no list showing through); keys stand before the label in their own
column (`⏎`, `/`, `ctrl-r`); a shadow may dim what is under it but never erase it (#29). No chevrons at the
choices, no pill buttons.

chrome-textselection.name: PaneFrame
chrome-textselection.description:
Text selected with the mouse (issue #51; Ratatui `select::paint`, Ink `app/selected.ts` over `input/selection.ts`):
gg captures the mouse, so the terminal cannot select text and the renderer does. A drag starts in the text of a pane
and selects from the press to the pane's right edge, every row between from edge to edge, then from the left edge to
the pointer, as a terminal's selection runs. It belongs to the pane it started in: the border, the title row and the
scrollbar are never part of it, and a pointer dragged outside stops at the pane's edge.

**Use it** through the host: a drag in a document, rich text, a log or the dock's transcript selects, a double-click
selects a word (a path or URL whole), a triple-click the line, shift+arrows extend, `ctrl+c` copies and any other key
or the wheel clears it. On rows (a list, tree, table) a double-click still opens, so a drag there does not select. A
part never draws a selection; it is a paint over the finished frame, like the hover.

**States:** a drag across two rows (the press to the edge, then the left edge to the pointer), and the mono tier.

**Rules:** the selected cells take `bg.selection` and keep their text colour and glyph; in the mono tier, where the
slot has no colour, they are reversed instead. The cells just outside the pane (its border and scrollbar, the rows
above and below the drag, the cells before the press and after the pointer) are never selected. While a drag selects,
the status line names the key for the terminal's own selection.

**Reference gap:** the scene records the drag (`view.selection`) but not which pane has the keys. The border colour
says: the log's is the accent (the keys), the detail pane's `accent.muted` (not), so the stories draw them so.
`test/app/selection-cells.test.tsx` makes the same drag in the whole App and compares every body cell's selection
background with these cells.

dock-dock.name: Dock
dock-dock.description:
The agent dock under the middle pane (host `DockView`, crates/radar-core/src/dock.rs; Ink only, `src/dock/Dock.tsx`;
Ratatui draws the one-line notice in its place). A frame holding the tab row (one tab per session: pack icon, name,
state; the one showing in brackets and bold accent, as the page tab row's), the transcript, the composer and the
status line. Every story draws a state the host recorded (ink/test/fixtures/dock, written by radar-core).

**Use it** through the host: a part supplies the dock's content, the host adds shown/focused/height and sends it on
every screen (backtick shows and focuses it, again hides it). Ink keeps no state of record; every key, click and
drag is an `Intent::Dock`.

**States:** empty, streaming (text marked by the running icon until saved), an answer in markdown (laid out as
ui::rich lays out a description, src/text/richRows.ts) and the same half received, tool calls one row each (kind
icon, verb, target relative to the session's folder, `+n −m` for an edit) folded to `⋯ n` and open with tree lines,
reads in a row folded into one row, an edit's diff opened, reasoning with its latest line while the session works,
an approval waiting, a question waiting, an error, stopped, a terminal tab (T7's surface); the activity line above
the composer (thinking, writing, running a command, waiting for your approval or answer, with the turn's time and
tokens; done, stopped or failed after it); each tab's state mark (spinner, needs you, failed, unread, not attached,
being read back); full height (`alt-f`); a session restored from the last run (lapsed requests and questions,
detached and resuming, `alt-r` and `/resume`).

**Rules:** no chevrons or `[+]`/`[-]` for folding; every mark is a pack icon; keys sit inside their word, underlined
(`a̲pprove once`, `d̲eny`, `v̲iew diff`), and a click on the word does what the key does; nothing is approved or
answered but by the user, and an approval shows the exact command, path or URL. A question's choices are numbered
(the number is the key, before the word), the composer's words answer one that takes them, esc declines.

dock-terminalview.name: TerminalView
dock-terminalview.description:
A program's own screen in a dock tab (`ink/src/terminal`, host side `crates/radar-sessions-pty`). The host runs the
program in a PTY and keeps its output; Ink parses the bytes (xterm's engine) and draws the cells. The pictures are
recordings of `less -R` made by the host's PTY, replayed as the host replays them to a renderer that attaches.

**Use it** in a dock tab whose `terminal` is set; the dock gives it the tab's content area and the keys while focused.

**States:** following a running program; the program ended (how it ended, `r̲estart`); at 80x24 and 160x40.

**Rules:** the program's colours are its own; the surface adds nothing but the ended row, whose key sits inside its
word. Ctrl+] gives the keys back. Ink only: Ratatui has no terminal tab.
